transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-21
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Marcus (Redwood AE), Sofia (Redwood SE), Ibrahim (Solutions), Anil, Priya, Lena, Tom
Shared: 2027-kestrel-console-deck.pdf (Google Drive link), route-cost-model.xlsx

[00:00] Marcus: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:03] Anil: yeah, we're good, thanks Marcus.
[00:06] Marcus: cool quick intro — I'm Marcus Bell on the AE side, Sofia here is our SE who will show the console and do the deeper route-level stuff. Ibrahim is on for any billing nuance.
[00:17] Sofia: hi all, nice to meet you. we'll go through per-route dashboards, usage analytics, and the cost breakdown flows, and then leave time for the finops questions.
[00:26] Priya: great, main ask is we want to map cost to our microsvc routes and see where the token spend is blowing up.
[00:31] Lena: and we need to reconcile that to monthly budget forecasts, so visibility at a route tag level is a hard requirement.
[00:38] Sofia: absolutely, that's what the route lens is for — we can show live telemetry, per-route token counts, latency, and a cost model that attributes spend to tags.
[00:47] Tom: quick security callout — data residency and audit logs. we need to confirm what gets logged in the consol and how long retention is.
[00:55] Marcus: noted, we'll share the SOC2 and ISO docs after the call, and we can show the audit log UI in the console.

[01:10] Sofia: alright I'm going to share my screen — (link) — ok this is the Redwood Consol — // subtle transcript note: 'Console' sometimes shows as 'Consol' —
[01:22] Sofia: first screen is the usage overview. top row you see aggregate tokens, requests per minute, and cost burn. you can filter by time range, by model family, or by route.
[01:34] Marcus: one thing we recommend is to instrument routes with consistent tags — that lets the console automatically rollup per-team or per-product views.
[01:42] Priya: how do routes get tagged? do we need SDK changes or is it headers?
[01:47] Sofia: both — the easiest is to set a route header in the Redwood API call, or you can map your ingress route in the console to our route id. SDK patches are optional.
[01:55] Priya: ok we prefer not to change all services right away. mapping in the console sounds better.

[02:12] Sofia: here's an example: Route "search-autocomplete" — you can see tokens in, tokens out, cost estimate, avg latency, and a 95th percentile. we also show the model used and quantization profile.
[02:26] Anil: that quantization thing — is it per-model or per-route? we run both a small quick model and a larger re-ranker.
[02:33] Sofia: you can pin a model per route, and the console supports variant profiles so you can say route X uses quantized t4-8bit for cheap runs and route Y uses a larger model for high-quality re-ranks.
[02:44] Anil: perfect. can we see side-by-side cost between hosted and dedicated? we'd like to evaluate dedicated pools for steady traffic.
[02:52] Ibrahim: yes we expose cost per deployment type — hosted API per-token, and a notional equivalent for Dedicated capacity to show per-hour amortized.
[03:01] Lena: how accurate is the per-token cost projection? finance needs to trust it for forecasting.
[03:07] Sofia: we use a configurable unit-cost model. you can plug in your committed sku rates for Dedicated and cloud egress assumptions. it's an estimate but we've seen it match within 5–10% of invoices when configured.

[03:25] Speaker 1: um there's a small pause as Sofia toggles views —
[03:29] Sofia: next we have the route breakdown page — you can expand a route and see the top prompt snippets (masked) that are driving tokens, and spike detection that highlights anomalies.
[03:42] Priya: spike detection — what's the sampling cadence? we have bursty traffic.
[03:47] Sofia: default is 5 minute buckets with configurable thresholds, you can also set alerts via webhook or pagerduty.
[03:54] Marcus: and we recommend a 5% sample of full payloads for prompt-level quality monitoring; everything's encrypted in transit and at rest.

[04:10] Anil: about caching — we have a lot of prefix reuse on autocomplete, can the console show cache hit rates?
[04:16] Sofia: yes, KV cache and prefix caches are surfaced per-route. you can see hit ratio and suggested cache TTLs; we also give a potential per-route savings estimate if you enable caching.
[04:27] Lena: nice, could we get a projection of monthly $ savings if we enable caching across the top 10 routes?
[04:33] Sofia: yes — the spreadsheet I sent includes a 'what-if' tab that runs those numbers from sampled traffic.

[04:45] Tom: on the audit side — where do audit logs live? can we ship them to our Splunk?
[04:50] Marcus: you can forward audit events to your SIEM via syslog or S3 export; the console also keeps an immutable audit trail for admin actions, retention is configurable up to X years per enterprise plan.
[05:05] Tom: ok we'll follow up with support on exact retention numbers.

[05:18] Sofia: switching to the 'cost explorer' view — this is where finance folks will live. you can group by route, model, or tag. you can also overlay budgets and see burn rates against monthly commits.
[05:30] Lena: can we export per-route daily CSV for our internal billing system?
[05:34] Sofia: yep CSV export or automated S3 delivery. we can also push to BigQuery for analytics.

[05:46] Priya: are there any gotchas with VPC/private deployment and console observability? we plan a VPC deployment next quarter.
[05:55] Sofia: for Private you run the inference nodes in your VPC; telemetry and metadata can be routed back to the private control plane or mirrored to your observability stack. there are options to keep sensitive payloads from leaving your network.
[06:07] Anil: does that change the pricing model?
[06:09] Marcus: Private has a licensing component and then infra cost; our console still provides the same route views but you control the storage and retention options. we can share a pricing appendix.

[06:25] [07:00] Sofia walks through an example alert: sudden token spike on route "chat-support" due to prompt regen loop.
[07:08] Sofia: you can configure automatic fallback to a cheaper model or to cached response if a route trips a guardrail.
[07:15] Priya: interesting, do those fallbacks require code changes?
[07:19] Sofia: no — fallback policies live in the console routing layer. you can set them per-route, and we have templated policies for latency vs cost-first.

[07:34] Ibrahim: on cost optimization — our Optimize toolkit will recommend batching and quantization settings per route based on traffic shape. it will also suggest KV cache keys when appropriate.
[07:45] Anil: is the optimize recommendation automated or a playbook?
[07:48] Ibrahim: both — auto-suggested profiles, and you can simulate the cost/latency tradeoff in the console before rolling out.

[08:00] [08:20] Slight crosstalk: Marcus and Lena discussing budget buckets.
[08:25] Lena: for our forecast I need committed vs variable split — can the console show that?
[08:30] Sofia: yes, the cost model can be toggled to show committed amortization (for Dedicated) and variable hosted spend. you can export those breakdowns.

[08:45] Priya: how do we instrument the re-ranker route which has long KV cache lifetime? tokens-out is low but tokens-in is huge, seems to skew, can we attribute quality cost?
[08:57] Sofia: we show tokens-in vs tokens-out and suggest a quality metric mapping; you can attach eval sets to routes to correlate cost with quality regressions.

[09:10] Anil: one operational question — if we pin new model versions, is there a canary rollout in the console?
[09:17] Sofia: yes, rollouts support canary percentages, A/B, and automatic rollback if latency or error rate exceeds thresholds.

[09:30] Marcus: ok i'm going to demonstrate a quick 'what-if' — selecting top 5 routes by spend and toggling quantization from 16-bit to 8-bit. you'll see immediate projected savings and an estimated quality delta.
[09:44] [09:50] Anil: that delta number — how do you compute quality delta?
[09:53] Sofia: it's based on historical evals plus model provider guidance; it's approximate but helpful for tradeoffs. we also let you tie in your own eval data.

[10:05] Tom: about compliance one more time — do logs include PII? we need to redact tokens or mask prompts.
[10:11] Sofia: prompts can be masked on ingestion; we support configurable PII filters and a redact-on-insert policy for sensitive routes.

[10:25] PRIYA: small typo in the console — the token meter shows 'tokns' sometimes — haha — noted for engineering.
[10:31] [laughs]

[10:35] Sofia: last section — alerts and workflows. you can wire alerts to Slack, PagerDuty, or a webhook; action items from alerts can create tickets in Jira via integration.
[10:47] Marcus: one recurring ask from customers is a monthly route chargeback report — we support templated PDFs that show per-team spend and the last 3 months trend.

[11:00] Anil: cool — if we wanted to pilot, what's the minimal scope?
[11:05] Marcus: typical pilot: onboard 3–5 routes, enable telemetry and route mapping, run a 48–72 hour baseline, then implement 1 optimization (caching/batching) and measure savings. it usually takes 2–3 weeks end-to-end.

[11:22] Priya: do you have recommended guardrails for rate limits? our burst windows can be big.
[11:28] Sofia: yes defaults are conservative; you can set per-route RPS, queue depth, and burst allowances. also we have backpressure hooks for clients.

[11:45] Marcus: i'll recap next steps and action items — we'll share the cost model spreadsheet and console links, Sofia will stand up the test tenant, Kestrel sends sample traffic, Tom follows up on compliance questions.
[11:57] Lena: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[12:00] Marcus: thanks, we'll follow up by email with dates.

End of transcript.
